outcome_intro: Ask your AI where a quote stands, what is on it, and whether any line sells below cost, then have it build or reprice the quote for you to review before anything is written. quotewerks-cli works against QuoteWerks Web using the real column names, previews every typed write, and keeps a local copy of your documents so margin, win-rate, pipeline and cost-drift questions are one command each.

instead_of_say.instead: Open QuoteWerks, run a Document Lookup to find what the client bought in March, then hand-key every line into a new quote.
instead_of_say.say: Copy quote 1042 into a new quote with 12 of the laptops at today's prices, and show me before you create it.

instead_of_say.instead: When a distributor changes cost, open every open quote and check each line on the Document Items tab.
instead_of_say.say: Which open quotes have lines whose cost moved at least 2% since we quoted them, and what does it do to margin?

instead_of_say.instead: Write a one-off script or build a report every time someone asks for margin by rep before a QBR.
instead_of_say.say: What was our margin by sales rep on orders over the last 90 days?

pain_points: Quoting from an inbound email ("12 more laptops like the ones in March, plus docks") means finding the old document and re-keying every line into a new one. An MSP account manager described exactly this in a request on the QuoteWerks support forum.
Answering "where does the Acme quote stand?" means leaving what you are doing to run a Document Lookup in QuoteWerks.
When distributor cost moves, every affected quote has to be opened and each line touched by hand, and the quotes nobody touched go out at a thinner margin than anyone intended.
Margin and win-rate questions for a QBR mean writing a script or building a report for each question.
The QuoteWerks Web REST API (beta) is generic table access. An AI handed a raw table endpoint has to guess the column names, and a wrong guess quietly produces a bad quote.

outcomes.question: Where does the Acme quote stand?
What is on quote 1042, line by line, with margin per line?
Is anything on this quote priced below cost or under 10% margin before it goes out?
What does an 18% margin on these laptops do to the quote? Show me before you change it.
Which open quotes are 30 days old or more, and who do I chase?
What is our quote win rate by rep over the last 90 days?
Which open quotes carry a cost that no longer matches our product database?
What moved in the quote pipeline this week?

different_vs_wrappers: The QuoteWerks Web REST API is generic table access, and the [Zapier QuoteWerks app](https://zapier.com/apps/quotewerks/integrations) works one record at a time (create a quote, create a line item, find a quote, react to a new document). This skill adds typed quote commands that use the real QuoteWerks column names, fills new lines from your product databases, previews every typed write before it is sent, and keeps a local copy of your documents so cross-document margin, win-rate, pipeline and cost-drift questions are one local query.
different_vs_vendor: QuoteWerks Web has its own AI agent, and this skill can ask it questions too (`agent ask`). What the skill adds is reach from the AI you already work in: previewed quote builds and repricing, a per-line audit before a quote goes out, and analysis across every mirrored document. It complements QuoteWerks Web; it does not replace it.
credentials_note: Your API key stays in your environment unless you save it with `quotewerks-cli auth set-token`, which writes it to the CLI's credentials file (mode 0600) until you run `quotewerks-cli auth logout`

faqs.a: Yes, on paid ChatGPT plans. ChatGPT connects to remote MCP servers over HTTPS, but quotewerks-mcp speaks HTTP natively: set `QUOTEWERKS_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN` to a bearer token, run `quotewerks-mcp --transport http`, and put its /mcp endpoint (http://127.0.0.1:7777/mcp by default) behind an HTTPS tunnel or your own reverse proxy. Step-by-step in the install guide.

faqs.q: Do I need to know how to code?
faqs.a: No. Paste one sentence into Claude Code or Codex and your agent does the install, or run a one-line installer. You enter your API key once.

Your data stays on your machine. The CLI, the MCP server and the local mirror all run locally, and the AI sees query results, not a bulk dump of your quotes. MSP Skills never bundles or transmits your API key.
Free. Apache-2.0 licensed. You pay only for whichever AI agent you already use.

faqs.q: Does it work with QuoteWerks Desktop?
faqs.a: It works with QuoteWerks Web through the QuoteWerks Web REST API at qwwapi.quotewerks.com, which QuoteWerks labels beta. It does not open a QuoteWerks Desktop database or use the desktop COM API.

faqs.q: What API key do I need, and can the AI change my quotes?
faqs.a: Create a key in QuoteWerks Web under Setup > Options > Zapier and API; the API requires a user with MasterRights. A key without Allow write access can read but cannot change anything (QuoteWerks answers writes with 403). Even with a write-enabled key, `docs create`, `items add`, `items reprice` and `requote` only preview until you add `--confirm`. The raw `tables insert`, `tables update` and `tables delete` commands send immediately, so keep the key read-only unless you need writes.

faqs.q: Will this hammer the QuoteWerks API?
faqs.a: No. margin, winrate, pipeline, cost-drift and changes read the local copy that `quotewerks-cli mirror` makes, so you can ask as many questions as you like without another API call. mirror reads 1,000 rows per request, and requests are paced to the server's rate-limit headers by default.

governance_summary: The skill reads your QuoteWerks Web quotes, orders, invoices, line items, product databases and settings, and it can create and change documents. The typed writes (`docs create`, `items add`, `items reprice`, `requote`) only preview until you add `--confirm`. The raw table writes (`tables insert`, `tables update`) send immediately, so preview them with `--dry-run` first, and keep `tables delete` and the credential commands for a human.

safety_tiers.examples: `docs search`, `docs get`, `docs lint`, `items list`, `products search`, the `tables` reads (`list`, `rows`, `row`, `query`, `schema`, `values`), the `cloud-settings` reads, `reports run`, `identity userinfo`, `agent ask` (and `import agent`, CLI only, which sends a JSONL file of questions to the same AI agent), and the mirror reports (`margin`, `pipeline`, `cost-drift`, `winrate`, `changes`); `mirror` and `sync` write only the local copy
`docs create`, `items add`, `items reprice`, `requote`: each previews by default and writes only with `--confirm` and a write-enabled key
safety_tiers.policy: Let the agent preview; a human approves before it re-runs with --confirm

safety_tiers.examples: `tables insert` and `tables update` (CLI only, never an MCP tool), which send immediately to any table your key can write
safety_tiers.policy: Preview with --dry-run, then a reviewed write

safety_tiers.examples: `tables delete` (CLI only; deletes a row in any table, documents included), `auth set-token`, `auth logout`
